The Petitioner, in the present Petition, has submitted that the Commission is explicitly vested with the authority to ensure the due execution and implementation of its own orders, including the order dated 7.11.2023 in Petition No. 270/MP/2022. It has been stated that the said power is drawn from Section 79 read with Section 94(1)(f) of the Act, which grants the Commission all the powers of a Civil Court for the purpose of executing its orders, and recovering the determined sums. The Petitioner has also contended that since the Respondents Discoms, have failed to comply with the order within the stipulated timeline of 30.11.2023, and have further admitted to an amount significantly less than the final adjudicated liability, the present Petition, filed under the inherent and statutory jurisdiction of the Commission, is necessary and maintainable to ensure the complete realisation of the decreed amounts, including payment of the principal LPS and the balance interest. Further, the Petitioner has outlined the discrepancies in the working/calculations of the Respondent Discoms as follows: However, the Respondent No.1 calculated interest on LPS from the date of payment till the date of the said order. Accordingly, the Petitioner has submitted that despite specific directions of this Commission regarding the payment of outstanding dues, the Respondent Discoms have failed to comply as (i) the outstanding LPS of Rs.24,27,48,694/- (as on 30.12.2023) is yet to be paid and (b) Outstanding interest on LPS of Rs.1,52,45,018/- is yet to be paid in full by the Respondent Discoms. Further, the Petitioner has submitted that, in terms of the order dated 7.11.2023, for the delay in making payment as per the timelines specified by this Commission, the Respondent Discoms are liable to pay LPS (at the rate specified in the POs) for the period of delay. Based on this, the total interest payable by the Respondent Discoms, pursuant to the said order (as on 30.11.2024) has been worked out as Rs. 3,64,04,430/-. In this background, the present Petition has been filed by the Petitioner, with the prayers as mentioned in para 1 above. 8. The Petition was admitted on 24.6.2025, and notices were issued to the Respondents, with directions to the parties to complete the pleadings in the matter. However, no reply was filed by the Respondent Discoms. 9 _._ During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner, while pointing out that the Respondents had not filed their replies, requested the Commission to grant one final opportunity to the Respondents to file the same. Accordingly, the Commission adjourned the matter, extending a last opportunity to the Respondents to complete pleadings in the matter. 10. During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Respondent Telangana Discoms submitted that they have already paid the outstanding amounts due to the Petitioner in terms of the Commission’s order dated 7.11.2023. In response, the learned counsel for the Petitioner sought liberty to file an affidavit, confirming the receipt of such payments and consequently, for the withdrawal of the present Petition. Considering this, the Commission reserved its order in the Petition, after permitting the Petitioner to file its affidavit, as aforesaid. _"4. I say that during the pendency of the Petition, the Respondents, TG Discoms and TGPCC approached the Petitioner with a proposal to settle the dispute. Post several rounds of discussions, the parties have agreed to settle the issue basis the agreement reached between the parties, as detailed hereunder: -_ _(c) On 16.10.2025, without prejudice to its rights and contentions, the Petitioner issued a revised counter proposal for settlement to TGPCC. In terms of the revised counter proposal, the Petitioner sought the following:_ _5. I say that the Petitioner is in receipt of the said amount. Therefore, it is requested that this Hon'ble Commission may dispose of the present Petition No. 336/MP/2025 in terms of the settlement between the parties (as detailed hereinabove), with liberty to the Petitioner to approach this Hon'ble Commission as and when the need arises."_ the Respondents have made the payments to the Petitioner, in terms of the settlement between the parties, the prayers of the Petitioner do not survive for consideration. The present Petition is disposed of accordingly. With regard to the Petitioners’ prayer for liberty to approach the Commission, as and when the need arises, we find no need to grant such prayer, considering the fact that the parties have settled the matter. Needless to say, the Petitioner is not prevented from approaching this Commission, in case of any fresh cause of action.
